title: Table XXV. Independent Benchmark Evaluation: CardDemo versus Masquerade

carddemo_benchmark.reference_implementation: Legacy CICS COBOL 85 (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2.0 compatibility harness + Python companion model)
carddemo_benchmark.execution_method: High-throughput companion runner cross-validated against WSL GnuCOBOL
carddemo_benchmark.adaptations: CICS BMS screen mapping, environment variable input ingestion, DFHEIBLK injection
carddemo_benchmark.limitations: Evaluates single-screen CICS transaction processing with fixed record schemas.

masquerade_benchmark.reference_implementation: Standard Batch COBOL 85 (WSL GnuCOBOL 3.1.2.0 binary + companion model)
masquerade_benchmark.execution_method: Native WSL GnuCOBOL compiled binary paired with high-throughput runner
masquerade_benchmark.adaptations: File assignment mapping (DALYTRAN, XREFFILE, ACCTFILE, TCATBALF, DALYREJS), dataclass repo bindings
masquerade_benchmark.limitations: Batch sequential processing; does not exercise asynchronous MQ triggers or IMS DB2.

empirical_comparison.precision_preservation: Identical (100.0% precision, 0 false alarms on equivalent controls across both systems)
cross_system_conclusions: BEACON's certification pipeline functions across distinct architectural domains: CICS Online Screen (CardDemo COACTUPC) and Batch Balance Accounting (Masquerade CBTRN02C).
Defect detection recall on Masquerade is 62.50% (vs 75.00% on CardDemo) under random input testing.
Precision remains 100.0% on both benchmarks, demonstrating that BEACON's sufficiency and mismatch gating produce zero false alarms on semantics-preserving refactorings across independent systems.
Subtle edge defects (<0.5% trigger probability) remain undetected by random black-box sampling in both benchmarks, underscoring the necessity of targeted concolic test generation.
